Marcus — thanks. Attaching the 7-day sample. High level: median prompt ~120 tokens, generation average ~350 tokens. About 60% of requests are interactive UI calls where p95 must be <= 250ms, rest are background batch jobs tolerating up to 1.5s. Peak qps last week hit 42 sustained for a 10-minute window; there are occasional microbursts up to ~140 qps for <1 min.

We'd like a committed plan that keeps the UI p95 inside 250ms even during 30-minute sustained increases (e.g., marketing pushes). Procurement is cc’d for timing — we’re targeting a July 1 start for dedicated capacity.

— Elena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Model run — baseline tokens/sec and SLA fit (draft)

Team — I ran a quick throughput estimate against SynapseRx's profile. Assumptions:
- Model: open-instruct-13B (quantized int8 path) — typical generation cost ~0.22 GPU-ms/token on A100-class SKU with our optimized kernels.
- Effective tokens per request (prompt + generation) = 470 tokens average.
- Target UI SLO: p95 <= 250ms maps to a per-request budget ~250ms wall time (including network + infer).

Preliminary numbers: sustained tokens/sec to keep p95 in budget (single GPU baseline) = ~900 tps. That supports ~1.9 requests/sec at 470 tokens/request while keeping p95 near 250ms.

To hit the observed 42 qps sustained, we need ~22 GPUs (900 tps/GPU * 22 = 19.8k tps → ~42 qps at 470 tokens). For microbursts up to 140 qps, plan a burst cushion of additional 28 GPUs (~50% extra) if we relied only on dedicated capacity.

Notes / mitigations:
- Priyom: enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (UI flows) could cut effective tokens/request by ~25% — reduces needed baseline GPUs to ~17.
- Ben: a fall-back to the cheaper int4-quantized model for non-critical batch workloads preserves headroom.

Action: I'll draft a committed-capacity recommendation that trades off baseline GPUs vs committed tokens plus burst pool.

Marcus

Subject: Re: Model run — baseline tokens/sec and SLA fit (draft)

Quick ops perspective: mapping to GPU SKUs and the Dedicated offering —
- For sustained 42 qps target we should use 80GB A100 equiv nodes (good balance of perf + KV cache capacity). 22 nodes is the right order.
- For a July 1 start, recommended commit: 18 nodes reserved + 6-node burst pool (pre-configured autoscale) — this reduces committed cost and gives a 30-40% cushion when combined with caching and quantization.
- Fallback rules: when latency >250ms on UI path, route non-critical gen to int4 instance group and shed batch to a best-effort pool. That keeps user-facing SLOs intact.

Cost note for Sales: 18-node reserved + burst usage pricing gives SynapseRx a predictable monthly commit with operational headroom; I’ll attach a short deck with the numbers.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Ben — procurement is reviewing the proposed commit. Two quick asks before sign:
1) Can you include SLA language that guarantees p95 UI path latency under the committed baseline, and an escalation path if we observe >3 SLA breaches in a rolling 30d window?
2) We'd like an explicit mapping of committed nodes to burst behavior (how credits are consumed and how fast autoscale provisions additional nodes).

We aim to finalize by end of next week; July 1 start is preferred. Please send the revised deck and an operational runbook link for our SRE team.

Procurement Team
SynapseRx

Summary (sent by Marcus Lin):
We recommend: 18 reserved 80GB-A100-equivalent nodes at launch, with a 6-node burst pool and KV caching + quantization enabled. Expected baseline support: ~42 qps sustained with p95 UI near 250ms after caching; microburst absorption (to 140 qps) requires burst pool + short-term autoscale. Next steps: finalize SLA wording, attach runbook and cost deck, align start date with procurement.
